lessons.title: **From Bits to Computers** — Describe the course's machine-building approach and the distinction between a model and a physical computer.
**Two-State Signals** — Explain logical states and why physical voltage or switch conventions must be defined.
**Bits and Bytes** — Reason about eight-bit patterns and their 256 possible states.
**Number Representations** — Convert selected unsigned values between binary, decimal, and hexadecimal.
**Codes and Meaning** — Explain how one byte can represent different things under different encodings.
**Addresses and Values** — Distinguish a memory location from the byte stored at that location.
**Boolean Logic** — Predict a gate's output from inputs using a truth table.
**NAND Construction** — Derive NOT and AND from NAND operations.
**Combining Gates** — Construct OR and XOR and explain intermediate signals.
**Circuit Description** — Represent a small circuit with a diagram or simulator.
**Circuit Verification** — Compare all Boolean input combinations with independently derived expectations.
**Clocked Storage** — Explain the difference between changing an input and committing stored state.
**Registers and Enables** — Predict an eight-bit register's value across active clock edges.
**Bus Selection** — Select one data source and explain contention when drivers conflict.
**Addressable Memory** — Trace controlled reads and writes to separate RAM locations.
**Bitwise Operations** — Apply NOT, AND, OR, XOR, and shifting to fixed-width patterns.
**Binary Addition** — Explain carries and eight-bit modular arithmetic.
**ALU Selection** — Trace how an operation selector chooses arithmetic or logic results.
**Zero Detection** — Predict when an eight-bit result sets the zero flag.
**ALU Debugging** — Use expected-versus-observed values to locate a computation fault.
**Processor Datapath** — Identify the roles of the PC, instruction decoder, accumulator, ALU, flag, and memory.
**Clock and Control** — Explain how decoded control signals cause state transitions.
**Fetch and Decode** — Trace a two-byte instruction from program memory to its operand.
**Execute and Commit** — Explain changes to the PC, accumulator, flag, and memory after an instruction.
**Instruction Encoding** — Distinguish opcodes, operands, and even-aligned instruction addresses.
**Data Movement** — Trace immediate loads, RAM reads, and permitted memory writes.
**Arithmetic Instructions** — Predict accumulator and zero-flag changes after ADDI and ANDI.
**Branches and Flags** — Compare JMP, taken JZ, and untaken JZ execution.
**Program Tracing** — Hand-assemble and trace short programs instruction by instruction.
**Invalid Instructions** — Explain unsupported opcodes, illegal addresses, and misaligned targets.
**Memory-Mapped I/O** — Explain why some addresses interact with devices rather than RAM.
**Input and Output** — Trace keyboard-input and display-output latch behavior.
**Polling and Interrupts** — Distinguish two device-notification approaches without assuming they exist in the reference machine.
**Storage and Files** — Relate persistent bytes, storage devices, and file-system abstractions.
**Firmware and Boot** — Distinguish program-image initialization from firmware, bootloader, and OS startup.
**Hardware and Software** — Separate CPU/device responsibilities from programs, drivers, and operating systems.
**System Connections** — Link gates, registers, ALU, memory, control, and device latches in an inspectable diagram.
**Program-to-Output Trace** — Follow initialized instruction bytes through state transitions to a device result.
**Fault Diagnosis** — Distinguish wrong bit order, arithmetic errors, invalid branches, and unavailable devices.
**Model Boundaries** — Defend what the simplified machine explains and what real systems additionally require.

outcomes.description: Explain two-state signals, bit patterns, byte values, encoding conventions, and the distinction between a memory address and its contents.
Construct basic Boolean gates from NAND logic and predict their behavior from complete truth tables.
Build and investigate clocked eight-bit storage, controlled bus transfers, and addressable memory.
Construct an eight-bit arithmetic/logic model and explain wraparound arithmetic, Boolean operations, and zero detection.
Encode and trace reference-machine instructions, including fetch/decode/execute, branching, memory effects, and explicit fault states.
Explain how memory-mapped devices, persistent storage, firmware, software, operating systems, and file systems relate without treating the teaching machine as a real OS.
Connect tested logic and storage components to a defensible end-to-end program-to-output trace, including assumptions, failures, and model limitations.
